rounds.prompt:
Write a file `policy.py` in the current directory containing a control policy for the
robotics domain described below.

The file must define exactly this function:

    def policy(observation):
        # See the observation schema below.
        # Return {"skill_index": <int>, "params": [<float>, ...]}.

`skill_index` indexes `observation["skills"]`, the ground skills whose preconditions
hold RIGHT NOW -- so any index in range names a legal action, and there is no way to
select something inapplicable. `params` must have exactly `param_dim` finite floats for
the skill you chose; a skill with `param_dim` 0 takes an empty list.

Only the standard library and `numpy` may be imported. The function must be
deterministic and fast: it is called once per environment step, thousands of times per
evaluation. Do not try to run the environment; it does not exist in this sandbox. The
policy is evaluated outside the sandbox and you will be told how it did.

The observation is a plain JSON-shaped dict:

    {
      "goal":    ["Predicate(obj, obj)", ...],   # atoms that must ALL hold to solve
      "objects": [{"name": str, "type": str, "features": {name: float}}, ...],
      "atoms":   ["Predicate(obj, obj)", ...],   # every atom true right now
      "skills":  [{"index": int, "name": str, "objects": [str, ...],
                   "param_dim": int}, ...]
    }

`goal` and `atoms` use the same rendering, so you can test goal satisfaction by string
membership. `objects` carries the raw continuous state; `atoms` is its symbolic
abstraction. Both are always present and consistent with each other.

## Object types (name, then its continuous features)

  robot(room, holding)
  room(index, blocks_right)
  trash_bin(count, room, kind, throw_distance)
  recycling_bin(count, room, kind, throw_distance)
  trash_button(room, kind)
  recycling_button(room, kind)
  trash(kind, weight)
  recycling(kind, weight)
  pile(room, weight_seed, num_pickups)

## Objects in this world

  robot: robot
  recycling_bin: recycling_bin
  trash_bin: trash_bin
  trash_button: trash_button
  recycling_button: recycling_button
  pile: pile
  trash: trash
  recycling: recycling
  room_0: room
  room_1: room
  room_2: room
  room_3: room
  room_4: room
  room_5: room
  room_6: room

## Predicates

  RobotInRoom(robot, room)
  HandEmpty(robot)
  HoldingTrash(robot, trash)
  HoldingRecycling(robot, recycling)
  Adjacent(room, room)
  TrashInBin(trash, trash_bin)
  RecyclingInBin(recycling, recycling_bin)
  TrashBinEmpty(trash_bin)
  RecyclingBinEmpty(recycling_bin)
  TrashBinInRoom(trash_bin, room)
  RecyclingBinInRoom(recycling_bin, room)
  TrashButtonInRoom(trash_button, room)
  RecyclingButtonInRoom(recycling_button, room)
  PileInRoom(pile, room)
  CanMoveRoom(room, room)

## Skills

  PickupTrash(?robot - robot, ?trash - trash, ?room - room, ?pile - pile)  [param_dim=0]
    preconditions: HandEmpty(?robot), PileInRoom(?pile, ?room), RobotInRoom(?robot, ?room)
    add effects: HoldingTrash(?robot, ?trash)
    delete effects: HandEmpty(?robot)

  PickupRecycling(?robot - robot, ?recycling - recycling, ?room - room, ?pile - pile)  [param_dim=0]
    preconditions: HandEmpty(?robot), PileInRoom(?pile, ?room), RobotInRoom(?robot, ?room)
    add effects: HoldingRecycling(?robot, ?recycling)
    delete effects: HandEmpty(?robot)

  MoveRoom(?robot - robot, ?from_room - room, ?to_room - room)  [param_dim=0]
    preconditions: CanMoveRoom(?from_room, ?to_room), RobotInRoom(?robot, ?from_room)
    add effects: RobotInRoom(?robot, ?to_room)
    delete effects: RobotInRoom(?robot, ?from_room)

  ThrowTrash(?robot - robot, ?trash - trash, ?trash_bin - trash_bin, ?room - room)  [param_dim=1]
    preconditions: HoldingTrash(?robot, ?trash), RobotInRoom(?robot, ?room), TrashBinEmpty(?trash_bin), TrashBinInRoom(?trash_bin, ?room)
    add effects: HandEmpty(?robot), TrashInBin(?trash, ?trash_bin)
    delete effects: HoldingTrash(?robot, ?trash), TrashBinEmpty(?trash_bin)

  ThrowRecycling(?robot - robot, ?recycling - recycling, ?recycling_bin - recycling_bin, ?room - room)  [param_dim=1]
    preconditions: HoldingRecycling(?robot, ?recycling), RecyclingBinEmpty(?recycling_bin), RecyclingBinInRoom(?recycling_bin, ?room), RobotInRoom(?robot, ?room)
    add effects: HandEmpty(?robot), RecyclingInBin(?recycling, ?recycling_bin)
    delete effects: HoldingRecycling(?robot, ?recycling), RecyclingBinEmpty(?recycling_bin)

  PressTrash(?robot - robot, ?trash_button - trash_button, ?room - room, ?trash_bin - trash_bin, ?trash - trash)  [param_dim=0]
    preconditions: RobotInRoom(?robot, ?room), TrashButtonInRoom(?trash_button, ?room)
    add effects: TrashBinEmpty(?trash_bin)
    delete effects: TrashInBin(?trash, ?trash_bin)

  PressRecycling(?robot - robot, ?recycling_button - recycling_button, ?room - room, ?recycling_bin - recycling_bin, ?recycling - recycling)  [param_dim=0]
    preconditions: RecyclingButtonInRoom(?recycling_button, ?room), RobotInRoom(?robot, ?room)
    add effects: RecyclingBinEmpty(?recycling_bin)
    delete effects: RecyclingInBin(?recycling, ?recycling_bin)

What a skill's continuous parameters MEAN, and what makes an action succeed, are NOT
given to you. The predicates and effects below say what a skill is supposed to achieve,
not how to achieve it. Where a skill takes parameters, finding the relationship between
the observable state and the parameter values that work is the actual problem -- reason
about it from the feedback you are given between rounds.
rounds.agent_text:
`policy.py` is written and exercised against synthetic observations (navigation, pickup, throw sweep, failure blacklisting, success attribution all behave).

**Symbolic controller** — parses `atoms` into predicate/arg tuples (no string-format assumptions beyond what's needed), builds the room graph from `CanMoveRoom` and navigates by BFS, so one-way doors are handled. Loop: if holding an item, empty its bin via the button if needed, walk to the bin room, throw; if hands are free, pick whichever outstanding goal item has the cheaper route from the pile room, pre-empty its bin, go to the pile, pick up. It also covers `TrashBinEmpty`/`RecyclingBinEmpty`/`RobotInRoom` goals, and never presses a button once the corresponding `*InBin` goal is satisfied (pressing would undo it).

**Throw parameter** — this is the unknown, so I made it adaptive rather than betting everything on one guess. Module-level state persists across steps and episodes. On each throw I record the bin's `throw_distance` d, the held object's `weight` w, and the param; on the next step I check whether the `*InBin` atom appeared (success), the object is still held (failure), or the robot moved rooms (likely an episode reset — sample discarded). Failed (d, w, param) triples are blacklisted, and exploration walks an ordered candidate list: first `d` itself, then `d·w`, `d/w`, `d·√w`, `d+w`, `d−w`, etc., then scaled variants, then a raw sweep. Once anything succeeds, it fits the family whose `param / f(d, w)` ratio is most constant across successes and predicts from that, falling back to exploration if the model starts missing.

The first action attempted is `param = throw_distance`, on the reading that the parameter names the throw distance directly. If that's wrong, the learner should find the right form within an evaluation — but the between-round feedback is what will actually pin down the functional form, so tell me what the score looks like and, if available, whether failed throws drop the object or leave it held.

`policy.py` is updated. Two changes; the symbolic controller (which was clean — MoveRoom 135/135, PickupTrash 7/7) is untouched.

**1. Repeated-call corruption, fixed.** The seven executed throws were consecutive entries 14–20 of my sweep list, so 14 candidates were consumed before the first throw the environment actually ran. The cause: the harness called `policy` many times on one unchanged observation, and my grader read each repeat as "still holding ⇒ that param missed." The policy now fingerprints the full observation (atoms plus every continuous feature); an identical fingerprint replays the cached action and records nothing. A verified side effect is that the policy is now deterministic under repeated calls on the same state, which it was not before. A reset guard (pile `num_pickups` decreasing) also discards samples that straddle an episode boundary.

**2. The throw parameter.** `p = 0.53·w` reproduces the lone success exactly and makes all six failures overshoots of 24–176%, so I lead with it (scaled by `d/2`, a no-op for the bins seen so far, both at `throw_distance` 2.0). The two rivals that also fit that single success — a weight-independent constant near 0.64 and a `√w` law — follow immediately, then coefficient sweeps of each class. Hypotheses are scored +1/−1 on outcome, highest score wins, ties broken by list order, so a wrong leader is dropped after one miss while a correct one accumulates and holds.

Replaying against five different assumed ground truths, each with the learner reset:

| assumed truth | hits/30 | first hit | last 10 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.53·w ±10% | 30 | attempt 1 | 10/10 |
| 0.62 const ±12% | 29 | attempt 2 | 10/10 |
| p ≤ 0.66 | 30 | attempt 1 | 10/10 |
| 0.45·w ±15% | 27 | attempt 4 | 10/10 |
| 0.58·√w ±10% | 26 | attempt 2 | 10/10 |

Every world converges and stays converged; the 15-duplicate-call variant of the first row is also 30/30.

The one thing the data cannot settle is whether the target scales with `throw_distance`, since both bins were at 2.0 — I assumed linear. If the next round varies `throw_distance` and the throw hit-rate drops on the bin with the new distance, that assumption is where to look.

`policy.py` is revised. The controller is unchanged (282/282 moves, 8/8 pickups, goals reached in both periods); both changes are in the throw learner.

**Phantom calls are no longer charged as misses.** The round‑1 throw used hypothesis #4, so four `ThrowRecycling` misses had been recorded against a skill the counters say ran exactly once — the harness calls `policy` more often than it steps the environment, and my signature guard only caught byte-identical repeats. The fix comes from your own data: `num_pickups` incremented on every throw in round 0, so a real throw always empties the hand, into the bin or onto the floor. An observation that still shows the object held is therefore not a miss, it's a call on a state that never advanced — it now records nothing (with a stall counter that concedes a miss after 8 unresolved calls, in case some regime does retain the object). Attempts are counted at grading time rather than at selection, so unstepped calls cost a hypothesis nothing, and `prev` is now keyed by episode via the pile's `weight_seed`, so interleaved tasks can't grade each other's throws.

**The parameter model tightened.** The two hits are `p/w` = 0.530 and 0.560 — stable to 5.6%, against 20% for a constant reading and 12% for √w. Decisively, `p = 0.7071` *failed* at w = 1.045, and that value sits dead-center of any constant model spanning both hits, so weight-independence is refuted outright rather than merely disfavored. Lead guess is now `p = 0.545·w·(d/2)`, within 3% of both hits, with every recorded miss ≥21% above it. The two hits are also consistent with a steeper `0.485·w^1.44` (both were heavy objects, where the laws agree), so that form and a shrunk-exponent compromise sit near the front, and a power-law regression takes over once five hits with enough weight spread pin the exponent down — gated on reproducing its own inputs to 8%, so hits from different regimes can't be blended into a bogus curve. Selection is by smoothed success rate with rank-dependent priors: one hit promotes a hypothesis, one miss demotes it, and a consistently landing one holds the lead.

Replaying 30 attempts against each candidate ground truth, learner reset each time:

| assumed truth | hits/30 | last 10 |
|---|---|---|
| 0.545·w ±8% | 30 | 10/10 |
| same, +5 phantom calls per step | 30 | 10/10 |
| 0.545·w ±4% (tight band) | 30 | 10/10 |
| 0.485·w^1.44 ±10% | 24 | 10/10 |
| 0.62·√w ±8% | 19 | 10/10 |
| 0.70 constant ±12% | 16 | 8/10 |
| p ≤ 0.60·w threshold | 30 | 10/10 |
| linear with 10% random failure | 26 | 10/10 |

Weakest case is a shallow exponent like `0.60·w^0.7` (18/30, 6/10 late) — it drifts between the √w and linear families. Runtime is 0.017 ms/call.

Still unresolved: every bin so far has had `throw_distance` 2.0, so the linear `d` scaling is still an assumption. If a test bin has a different distance and the hit rate drops only on that bin, that's the cause.

`policy.py` is revised. The controller is untouched again (429/429 moves, 9/9 pickups, 3/3 goals); both changes target the throw learner.

**The parameter estimate is now well-pinned.** Three landed throws give `p/w` = 0.530, 0.560, 0.530, and every miss was at `p/w` ≥ 0.658. So the confirmed-good interval is at least [0.530, 0.560]·w, and the lead guess `0.545·w` sits inside it with ~2.8% margin to either observed edge — no change needed there.

**The remaining phantom miss is closed off.** Round 2's throw used hypothesis #1 rather than #0, so index 0 had been demoted by a recorded miss, yet `ThrowRecycling` ran twice and hit twice. Since a real miss drops the object where it was thrown, I now only count a miss from a state that could actually be the step right after the throw — same room, same `num_pickups`, same object weight. A hand-empty state from a re-run of the same task instance (same `weight_seed`, which is why my episode key didn't separate them) fails that test and is ignored. I also gave index 0 enough prior weight, on the strength of its three hits, to survive one contradicting report and only step aside after a second.

Replaying the exact round‑2 observation now returns 0.546 instead of 0.531, and injecting the leak that caused the demotion leaves it unchanged.

Simulated 30 attempts per assumed ground truth, learner reset each time:

| assumed truth | hits/30 | last 10 |
|---|---|---|
| 0.545·w ±8% | 30 | 10/10 |
| same, +5 phantom calls, +2 leaked states per step | 30 | 10/10 |
| 0.545·w ±4% | 30 | 10/10 |
| only [0.53, 0.56]·w accepted (strictest reading of all 10 points) | 30 | 10/10 |
| 0.485·w^1.44 ±10% | 23 | 10/10 |
| 0.62·√w ±8% | 18 | 10/10 |
| 0.70 constant ±12% | 15 | 8/10 |
| p ≤ 0.60·w threshold | 30 | 10/10 |
| linear with 10% random failure | 26 | 10/10 |

Runtime 0.017 ms/call; output stable across 20 repeat calls on one state.

Two things I still can't settle from the data: every bin so far has had `throw_distance` 2.0, so the linear `d` scaling remains an assumption, and all three hits came from a single ~0.53–0.56 slice, so if the true band is narrower than that slice in some weight regime the fallback sweep (not the lead guess) would carry it.

rounds.agent_text:
`policy.py` is revised. Two changes.

**The round‑3 failure is fixed.** That period pressed `PressRecycling` once and then never picked up or threw — 148 moves of wandering. Cause: my hand-empty branch emptied the destination bin *before* fetching the item, and rooms with `blocks_right` are one-way (`CanMoveRoom` has `room_3→room_2` but not `room_2→room_3`). Detouring left to the button put the pile permanently out of reach. The policy now fetches the item first and presses afterward — legal, since pressing has no precondition on the hand — and only presses first when a reachability check over the waypoint sequence shows that's the ordering that keeps everything reachable. The same check guards the carrying branch's detour to the button. Verified on the reconstructed scenario: at room_4 it now heads for the pile, at the pile it picks up rather than walking to the button, and it presses on arrival while holding.

**The parameter list is now top-loaded instead of pointed.** Round 4's throw landed at `p/w = 0.515` from hypothesis #4 — the third round running where phantom misses pushed the policy several slots down before its one executed throw. I can't fully identify the mechanism, so rather than keep hardening the attribution, the first eight entries are now *all* inside the confirmed-good band (θ = 0.5375, 0.530, 0.545, 0.520, 0.555, 0.515, 0.560, 0.535), each with enough prior weight to absorb two contradicting reports. Being pushed down the list now costs nothing.

The band is well-supported: four successes at `p/w` = 0.515, 0.530, 0.530, 0.560 (8.7% spread) against a lowest failure of 0.658. The √w reading would need a band 24% wide whose top edge sits within 5% of a known failure, and the constant reading is refuted outright — `0.7071` failed between two successes. Lead value is now the band midpoint, `0.5375·w·(d/2)`.

Simulations, 30 attempts each, learner reset:

| assumed truth | hits/30 | last 10 |
|---|---|---|
| band [0.515, 0.560]·w (spans all 4 real hits) | 30 | 10/10 |
| 0.5375·w ±3% | 30 | 10/10 |
| d-scaled, bin at distance 4 | 30 | 10/10 |
| +5 phantom calls per step | 30 | 10/10 |
| 0.485·w^1.44 ±10% | 11 | 3/10 |
| 0.62·√w ±8% | 10 | 1/10 |

The last two rows are the deliberate cost: the eight cluster slots are wrong in those worlds, so recovery is slow. I took that trade because the linear reading is the only one consistent with all ten data points. If a test round shows throws missing at `p/w ≈ 0.5375`, that bet is what to revisit — and the most likely reason would be a bin with a `throw_distance` other than 2.0, since every bin seen so far has had exactly 2.0 and the linear `d` scaling is still untested against real data.
